data.one_liner: Manually expand the tap area of a widget without changing its size or layout.
data.what_it_does: Provides a widget called ExpandTapWidget that allows developers to increase the touch target size of a small widget using padding. It adheres to guidelines like Apple's 44x44px and Android's 48x48dp minimum targets without modifying the layout size.
use_when: You need to make a small icon or button easier to tap without increasing its visual layout size
You want to meet minimum touch target guidelines (like Apple or Material Design) for small widgets
avoid_when: The expanded area exceeds the boundary of the Parent Box unexpectedly
You already handle gestures at multiple conflicting parent/child levels without careful arrangement
strengths: Does not change the widget's size or layout
Includes a debug flag (debugPaintExpandAreaEnabled) to display the actual expanded area
weaknesses: Expanded area cannot exceed the boundary of the Parent Box
Requires careful placement to avoid gesture conflicts when wrapped inside or outside other GestureDetectors
data.minimal_example:
ExpandTapWidget(
  onTap: () {},
  tapPadding: EdgeInsets.all(25.0),
  child: smallWidget(),
)
